extracted.subtask_description: A national code setting ethical standards and requirements for journalists and news organizations, covering accuracy, fairness, independence, integrity, and respect in reporting and newsroom conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble — purpose and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: An informed public is vital to a democratic society. Canadian journalism’s purpose is to serve the public interest. It is our responsibility to act independently, to be fair and respectful, and to report the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Code of Ethics is based on more than a century of journalistic experience and represents our membership’s guiding principles. We welcome its adoption by all practicing journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy — commitment to accurate and reliable journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: We are committed to journalism in the public interest that is accurate and reliable. Journalists will strive to verify facts and put them in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and confidentiality of sources (1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will attribute news sources on the record whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sources will be kept confidential only when there is overriding public interest and when sources risk retribution or other serious harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update and correct throughout story lifecycle (1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy requires updating and correcting news and information throughout the life cycle of a news story as we become aware of relevant and reliable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and unambiguous correction of errors (1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors and inaccuracy that affect the understanding of a news story will be unambiguously and promptly corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify third-party and user-generated content (1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The commitment to accuracy also applies to verifying third party or user-generated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness — impartial, unbiased journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: We are committed to impartial, unbiased journalism that serves the public interest through the free and open exchange of ideas, and respects the diversity of society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid personal bias; separate commentary from news (2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should be fair and balanced, and avoid allowing their personal biases to influence their reporting. News events and public issues may be analyzed and put into context, but commentary, opinion or editorializing must be kept distinct from regular news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly distinguish news from advertising/sponsorship (2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will clearly distinguish news content from advertising and other forms of sponsorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report demographic characteristics only when relevant (2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Race, ethnicity, nationality, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, age or mental or physical disabilities will only be reported when relevant to news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be responsive to public questions of fairness (2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should be responsive to questions of fairness posed by the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence — act in the public interest; resist interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism’s first obligation is to act in the public interest. We will resist any attempts at censorship or interference, direct or indirect, which would undermine the principle of editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose corporate, political or other attempts to influence decisions (3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will oppose any corporate, political or other attempts to influence our journalistic decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse payments, gifts or favours for coverage (3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will pay our own way and not accept payments, gifts or favours in exchange for news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pay subjects or sources with a vested interest (3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not pay subjects or sources that have a vested interest in a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentators or contracted experts are exempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply same standards when reporting about owners; resist owner influence (3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will apply the same journalistic standards of fairness and balance when reporting news about owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will oppose attempts by owners, either directly or indirectly, to influence news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity — avoid conflicts of interest; disclose when unavoidable
rubrics_metrics.description: We will govern ourselves on and off the job in a manner that avoids conflict of interest, real or perceived. When conflicts are unavoidable, they should be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deception and misrepresentation unless public interest (4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: We avoid deceiving the people we cover or misrepresenting ourselves in any way, unless it is clearly in the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify rehearsed or recreated parts of coverage (4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: We identify clearly any part of our news coverage which is rehearsed or recreated.

rubrics_metrics.name: No plagiarism; proper attribution of others' work (4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Never plagiarize. We give proper attribution to the research, words, ideas, images, sound and intellectual property of others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise care with personal opinions and social media (4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: We recognize that expressing personal opinions publicly or in social media can erode our ability to be perceived as fair and balanced in our news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It affects our personal reputations and those of our news organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect — conduct respectful; consider editorial relevance and public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Our conduct will be respectful, always taking into account editorial relevance and the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect dignity, especially for children and the vulnerable (5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will endeavor to respect the dignity of everyone, especially when news involves children and the vulnerable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sensitivity and restraint with dangerous situations and graphic content (5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will act with sensitivity and restraint when reporting on potentially dangerous situations and when using violent or graphic images and descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat people with decency; avoid distorting events by presence (5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will treat people with decency, courtesy and consideration and we will strive not to distort the character or importance of events by our presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensationalism (5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will avoid sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect privacy unless overriding public interest (5.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not infringe on a person’s privacy unless we believe there is overriding public interest.
